transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start Time: 11:00 AM PDT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ava Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (OrionBridge Head of Partnerships), Meera Rao (Cloud Solutions Lead), Derek Wu (CTO)

Summary:
Quick partner intro + discovery between Redwood and OrionBridge (cloud/GPU partner). Discussed integration surfaces (marketplace vs SI-led deployments), pilot sizing, security/compliance asks, and next steps for a joint pilot and GTM motions. Shared links: partner deck (link), quick benchmark template (link).

Topics:
- Partner GTM and revenue splits
- Technical integration: Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC/private deployments, KMS/HSM, SSO
- Pilot scope: workloads, model sizes, latency targets, benchmarking plan
- Legal/process: MSA, channel reseller terms

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate the time. This is Samir from Redwood, I'm AE on the partnerships team, and with me is Ava, our solutions engineer. Quick check on audio?
[00:12] Liam: Audio's good. Hi Samir, thanks, Liam here. Excited to dig in.
[00:16] Ava: Hi all.
[00:18] Derek: Morning, Derek here.
[00:20] Meera: Hey, Meera.
[00:25] Samir: Cool. Quick agenda, we wanted to learn about OrionBridge's partner model, your infra and go-to-market, and see where Redwood's serving/runtime and partner program might fit. We'll do a brief intro to Redwood, then Ava will go a bit deeper on the technical surfaces and pilot options. Sound good?
[00:40] Liam: Yep, that's perfect. We are trying to build an ecosystem of cloud and GPU vendors and SIs to resell and co-sell. We liked Redwood's focus on inference and the Dedicated offering.
[00:50] Samir: Great. Super high level: Redwood provides hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem. We focus on production economics — latency, cost, reliability — and have tooling for observability and rollouts.
[01:05] Meera: Quick question up front, do you have a partner reseller model or more of a referral / technology integration?
[01:12] Samir: Flexible. We do both — marketplace/reseller for partners who want managed offerings, and SI or OEM integrations for partners that want to embed or operate. We can talk GTM later but we do revenue share for certain channels.
[01:25] Liam: Good. From OrionBridge side we operate a marketplace and also do managed private stacks for enterprise customers — often we install in their VPC or our cloud region. Primary ask is: will Redwood fit into both flows?
[01:38] Ava: Yes, we support both. For marketplace/reseller flows the Hosted API is easiest. For managed/private installs we have Redwood Private and Dedicated which can be deployed into partner or customer VPCs, integrate with KMS, and we support SAML/SSO and audit logs.
[01:55] Derek: On the private deployments — how opinionated is the infra? We run mixed clusters — A100, H100, and some L2 iGPUs for inference. We need a runtime that picks kernels per hardware and supports quantization.
[02:10] Ava: Yep, that's exactly what the runtime does: kernel selection, attention optimizations, and quantization-friendly paths. We also do KV cache management and prefix caching to reduce token cost. One caveat — some model variants need specific CUDA/cuDNN versions; we'll surface compatibility.
[02:28] Meera: For enterprise customers we have strict compliance — SOC 2 and ISO coming soon — they'll want encryption at rest, customer-managed keys, and auditability. How mature is Redwood's security stack?
[02:40] Samir: We have SOC 2 in our hosted environment, and for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and central audit logs. We also have RBAC and SSO. We'll share the security pack after.
[02:52] Liam: Awesome. Two parallel questions: 1) Pilot — what does a typical partner pilot look like? 2) Pricing — for Dedicated/reseller flows what's the rough economics?
[03:03] Ava: Typical pilot is small: reserved capacity for 2-4 weeks, we run a benchmark using your workload (we have a spreadsheet template), measure latency, throughput, and cost per token, then iterate on batching/quantization. For pricing we offer partner discounts during pilot and different models (commit-based for Dedicated, usage for Hosted).
[03:22] Derek: For benchmarking, can we run on our H100 fleet? We want to test a 70B model and an LLM re-ranking workload. Latency target is p95 < 250ms for single-turn queries.
[03:35] Ava: Yes, we can support H100. For the 70B model we'll likely recommend a quantized variant depending on accuracy requirements. For p95 <250ms we may need to tune batch size and do some prefix caching. We'll need your trace-level QPS and sequence lengths.
[03:50] Meera: On the integration side, is there a lightweight way for our sales team to demo — like a managed route they can provision quickly for a PoC?
[04:00] Samir: Absolutely. We can spin up a sandbox Dedicated or provide hosted API keys with restricted quotas to run quick demos. For reseller flows we can issue partner-managed keys.
[04:10] Liam: A couple of other notes — we work with several infra vendors, and they care about margins. How transparent is Redwood on kernel-level performance and unit economics?
[04:21] Ava: We have per-token cost breakdowns and trace-level latency dashboards in Redwood Console. We can also provide model performance profiles that have throughput/latency numbers per hardware. That helps partners set margins.
[04:35] Liam: Perfect. On the competitive side some partners ask how Redwood compares to Lambda Labs and PlexiCloud who offer similar stacks. How do you position?
[04:45] Samir: We emphasize production-first tooling and unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private. Also our routing/fallback policies and quality monitoring tied to evals. But yeah, there are overlaps — consider that in the notes.
[04:58] Derek: Any blockers with onboard — networking-wise? We have customers that require direct connect / private link and strict ingress/egress rules.
[05:08] Ava: Supported. We support VPC peering, private link, and customer-managed networking for Private deployments. For hosted we can work with partner VPNs and restricted IPs.
[05:18] Meera: Legal — channel terms and MSA. Do you have a partner MSA or do we need to run your enterprise MSA?
[05:25] Samir: We have a partner program MSA and reseller addendum. We'll share a redlineable version. Liam, we'll loop in legal as a next step.
[05:34] Liam: Sounds good.
[05:36] [06:00] Samir: I want to capture success criteria for a pilot — what does success look like from OrionBridge?
[06:08] Liam: For us, success is twofold: technical — meeting latency and throughput targets on our infra and proving we can manage margins; and commercial — a clear path to list Redwood-based offerings in our marketplace and sign at least one reseller contract within 90 days.
[06:25] Meera: From product side, we want an integration that allows our customers to choose between Hosted (fast) and Private (managed) options and a clear upgrade path.
[06:36] Derek: Tech success: p95 <250ms on target workloads and stable KV cache behavior under sustained QPS. Also end-to-end monitoring so we can triage.
[06:50] Ava: Good, we'll map those to pilot KPIs.
[07:00] [10:00] Liam: On the GTM side, what materials do you provide for partners?
[10:10] Samir: Partner playbooks, deal registration, co-marketing funds for strategic partners, and a partner portal. We'll share the partner one-pager and GTM deck.
[10:22] Liam: Nice. How do you handle support — do partners get a single point of contact?
[10:28] Samir: Yes, partner success managers plus SE on the account. For Dedicated we also have support SLAs on incidents.
[10:36] Liam: A note on margins — some infra vendors want transparent cost-per-GPU metrics so they can price their managed offering. Can you provide that?
[10:45] Ava: We provide cost breakdowns but we can also run a joint spreadsheet to populate per-GPU and per-token numbers for your partner-managed stack.
[10:55] Derek: We would like to run an internal technical spike before committing to a co-managed pilot. Who do we loop in?
[11:02] Ava: Loop Derek and your infra lead — Meera already here — and we'll need access to a small set of test instances and a model artifact. We'll run a 2-week spike.
[11:12] Meera: On data residency, some customers require EU-only. Does Redwood have regional deployments and data residency controls?
[11:20] Samir: Yes, we have hosted regions in NA and EU, and Private deployments can be placed in-region to satisfy residency. We'll capture requirements case-by-case.
[11:31] Liam: Any integration work for marketplace listing? Do you have a marketplace API or is it manual?
[11:38] Samir: We have an API for provisioning and also a manual onboarding flow for marketplace listings. Lots of partners use the API for automation.
[11:45] [18:00] Derek: A few low-level questions — runtime supports model quantization and fallback to smaller variants? And how do you handle KV cache eviction on rolling deploys?
[18:12] Ava: Runtime supports quantization and can fallback to smaller model variants automatically based on policy. Eviction: we persist KV cache to a local store with warming strategies; on rolling deploys we do staged warming and can maintain cache affinity per instance. Sometimes the transcription says KV "cash" or "cache" depending on audio so sorry for that.
[18:32] Derek: Good. What about GPU drivers and dependency management?
[18:36] Ava: We recommend standard driver stacks but for Private we can containerize and pin drivers; we also have a compatibility matrix.
[18:44] Liam: Last item — do you have references of partners who have done reseller listings?
[18:50] Samir: Yes, we can share 2-3 references; I'll include those in the follow-up.
[18:56] Meera: Great.
[19:00] [25:00] Samir: Ok let's recap and next steps — action items: I'll share partner deck, GTM one-pager, and security pack. Ava will schedule a tech deep dive with Derek and crew to scope the 2-week spike. OrionBridge will share infra diagram and pilot sizing numbers. Liam will intro legal and channel ops. Anything else?
[19:20] Liam: That covers it. Also, please include a quick benchmark template so our infra partners can plug numbers.
[19:28] Samir: Will do.
[19:32] Ava: We'll also include a sample benchmarking spreadsheet and recommended models to test.
[19:37] Derek: Thanks.
[19:40] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[19:45] Liam: Thanks Samir.

Notes: occasional transcription issues: proper nouns and product names may be slightly off (e.g., 'KV cash', 'Redwood Dedicated' heard as 'Redwood dedicate'); timestamps approximate. Links shared: partner deck (https://redwood.example/partner-deck), benchmark template (https://redwood.example/benchmark-template).

End of call.
